items.title: Anchoring vs. a real floor: what actually decides the final number?
items.description: Renata's final settlement wasn't purely a function of her opening ask, and it wasn't purely a function of her walk-away point either — both mattered. This models a simplified version of that pull: Ashgrove's realistic counter-midpoint (absent any anchoring) sits around $178,000, but Renata's own stated anchor pulls the eventual settlement toward it, while her walk-away point acts as a hard floor no negotiated number falls below. Drag her opening ask and her walk-away point to see where the settlement actually lands. The market P50 for her role is $195,000, P75 is $215,000, for reference.
items.compute: const companyMidpoint = 178000; const anchorPull = 0.65; let settlement = companyMidpoint * (1 - anchorPull) + params.statedAnchor * anchorPull; settlement = Math.max(settlement, params.batnaFloor); settlement = Math.min(settlement, 225000); return { settlement };
